who: GPT-6 Astra Pro, distributed compile review
what: PR85 source acceptance run 46083117935 rejected the unchanged distributed resolution simulation helper with E0502, although pinned Rust accepted it. All 130 existing core tests executed and passed; four new controls were not built, so later source suites and the final receipt check did not run. Original artifact 15240647237 matched SHA-256 2c471eeb7c9293f6325ee5cecb8e43de0925e7da9198b7f4e0d57f3770cf6011.
cost: The four real-source admission controls cannot qualify. The same missing scope in execution lowering can delay an operand temporary's destructor until after a later operand has run.
cause: Lazy Boolean operands are lowered without their own temporary-scope boundaries. The shared borrow carried by committed_packs(...).unwrap().is_some() is kept drop-live until the surrounding if ends, across the following mutable lease call. The existing two-phase activation check correctly rejects that overlong lowered lifetime.
whys: Blaze rejected the shared lookup followed by a mutable operation in a short-circuit condition.
The Option containing an opaque iterator was still drop-live when the later mutable receiver activated.
Borrow-flow lowering cleaned the temporary only after the entire if condition, rather than after its Boolean operand.
The lazy-Boolean paths in borrow-flow and executable lowering omitted operand-local temporary scopes; flattened let chains also need to distinguish ordinary Boolean links from pattern scrutinees.

Existing condition and borrow controls did not require an owned reference-carrying operand temporary to finish before a sibling operand, with observable destructor order and a genuinely live-borrow negative.
class: lowered control flow omits language-defined temporary lifetime boundaries
prevention: Give ordinary lazy operands explicit scopes in both lowerings, keep Boolean destinations alive outside those scopes, and preserve let-chain scrutinees and bindings. Add causal borrow-acceptance and actual destructor-order controls plus a live-borrow rejection; retain the unchanged distributed helper as full source acceptance. The Rust Reference specifies each lazy Boolean operand as a temporary scope: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes.
fix: Borrow-flow BranchOperand preserves the Boolean outside each operand's temporary scope, closes the scope, then branches. Structural traversal stays linear. Executable lowering uses the existing open/close machinery for both lazy operands and ordinary Boolean links in let chains; pattern scrutinees retain their condition/body scope. The existing temporary-lifetime integration target now checks six valid cases and three genuinely live E0502 controls with completed borrow checking, and executes a shared destructor-order oracle. The distributed helper and all loan/conflict rules remain unchanged.
state: Source repair and independent review complete. Exact-tree qualification is recorded with PR85 and is required before merge: the unchanged distributed source suite, the reduced ARM64 borrow controls, and identical executable fixture bytes on the frozen old compiler and the new compiler.
